items.q: She *works* in a hospital.
items.why: works = V1 + -s, no helper verb → Present Simple.

items.q: Look — they *are dancing*!
items.why: am/is/are + -ing → Present Continuous.

items.q: I *have visited* Turkistan twice.
items.why: have/has + V3 → Present Perfect.

items.q: She *has been waiting* for an hour.
items.why: have/has + been + -ing → Present Perfect Continuous.

items.q: We *met* at university.
items.why: V2, no helper verb → Past Simple.

items.q: I *was reading* when you called.
items.why: was/were + -ing → Past Continuous.

items.q: They *had left* before we came.
items.why: had + V3 → Past Perfect.

items.q: It *had been snowing* all night.
items.why: had + been + -ing → Past Perfect Continuous.

items.q: I think you *will like* this film.
items.why: will + V1 → Future Simple.

items.q: At noon we *will be travelling*.
items.why: will + be + -ing → Future Continuous.

items.q: By June she *will have finished* school.
items.why: will + have + V3 → Future Perfect.

items.q: By May I *will have been living* here for a year.
items.why: will + have + been + -ing → Future Perfect Continuous.

items.q: Listen! The baby is crying.
items.why: Happening right now → a process around NOW.

items.q: I left the party at midnight.
items.why: One finished action at a definite past time → a single point in the past.

items.q: I've lost my keys, so I can't get in.
items.why: A past action with a result now → an arc from the past to NOW.

items.q: At this time tomorrow I'll be flying to Astana.
items.why: In progress at a future moment → a process around a future point.

items.q: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
items.why: A scientific fact → Present Simple. Water = it → boils.

items.q: My sister ___ in a bank. She's a cashier.
items.why: A permanent job → Present Simple. She → works (no am/is before V1).

items.q: Aliya usually ___ to bed at eleven.
items.why: A routine with usually. She + go → goes (-es after o).

items.q: My parents ___ meat.
items.why: They → don't + V1.

items.q: Arman is very punctual. He ___ late.
items.why: Frequency adverbs go AFTER am/is/are: is never.

items.q: Timur speaks Chinese.
items.why: he/she/it → doesn't + V1. The -s moves to does: speak, not speaks.

items.q: They live near the university.
a: Do they live near the university?
items.why: Question: Do + they + V1?

items.a: Does the film start at eight?
items.why: Timetables use Present Simple. Does + subject + V1 (no -s).

items.q: He don't like coffee.
items.why: He → doesn't + V1.

items.q: The train leaves at 6:40 tomorrow morning.
o: It's a fixed timetable for the future
It's a decision made at this moment
items.why: Present Simple can describe official timetables, even for the future.

items.q: First you ___ this button, and then the machine starts.
items.why: Instructions and steps use Present Simple.

items.q: Look! It ___ outside.
items.why: Look! → happening now → am/is/are + -ing.

items.q: I ___ with my cousin this month while my flat is being repaired.
items.why: A temporary situation (this month) → Present Continuous.

items.q: Shh! The baby ___.
items.why: Right now → is + -ing.

items.q: Prices ___ very fast these days.
items.why: A change in progress (these days) → are + -ing. rise → rising.

items.q: We are watching the news.
a: We are not watching the news.
items.why: Negative: am/is/are + not + -ing.

items.q: Dana is working from home today.
a: Is Dana working from home today?
items.why: Question: Is + subject + -ing?

items.a: What are you doing this weekend?
items.why: Asking about arrangements → Present Continuous.

items.q: Why do you wear a coat? It's really warm today.
items.why: About this moment, not a habit → are you wearing.

items.q: I am knowing the answer.
items.why: know is a state verb — not used in the continuous: I know.

items.q: My brother is always borrowing my charger without asking!
o: The speaker is annoyed by a repeated action
It's a plan for the future
It's happening only at this second
items.why: always + Present Continuous often shows annoyance.

items.q: Sorry, I can't talk — I ___ dinner and my hands are dirty.
items.why: In progress at the moment of speaking → am cooking.

items.q: I ___ my keys, so I can't open the door.
items.why: A past action with a result now (no keys now) → have + V3.

items.q: Have you ever ___ kymyz?
items.why: Life experience: have + V3 (try → tried).

items.q: I've lived in Almaty ___ five years.
items.why: for + a period (five years); since + a starting point (2019).

items.q: We ___ each other since 2018.
items.why: From the past until now with since; know is a state verb → have known.

items.q: The film ___ — sit down quickly!
items.why: Very recent news with just → has just + V3.

items.q: She ___ three emails this morning, and it's only 10 a.m.
items.why: Unfinished time (this morning, still morning) → has + V3. write → written.

items.q: I have finished my essay.
a: I have not finished my essay yet.
items.why: Negative + yet: haven't + V3 … yet.

items.q: He has been to Shymkent.
a: Has he ever been to Shymkent?
items.why: Question: Has + subject + V3?

items.a: This is the first time I have flown.
items.why: It's the first time … → Present Perfect. fly → flown.

items.q: I have seen her yesterday.
items.why: yesterday = finished, definite time → Past Simple, not Present Perfect.

items.q: Oh no, I've left my phone at home!
o: A past action with a result now
An action at a finished past time
items.why: The result matters now: I don't have my phone.

items.q: I'm tired because I ___ all morning.
items.why: A recent activity that explains the present (tired) → have been + -ing.

items.q: How long ___ for the bus?
items.why: How long … up to now? → have/has been + -ing.

items.q: It ___ since lunchtime.
items.why: An action continuing from a starting point (since) → has been + -ing.

items.q: The kids are covered in mud because they ___ in the garden.
items.why: Visible evidence of a recent activity → have been + -ing.

items.q: Your eyes are red. Have you ___?
items.why: Evidence (red eyes) → Have you been + -ing?

items.q: He has been sleeping well lately.
a: He has not been sleeping well lately.
items.why: Negative: hasn't + been + -ing.

items.q: Arman has been working here for three years.
a: How long has Arman been working here?
items.why: How long + has + subject + been + -ing?

items.a: We have been looking for a flat since March.
items.why: Duration up to now: have been + -ing + since.

items.q: I have been knowing him for ten years.
items.why: know is a state verb → Present Perfect Simple: have known.

items.q: I've been reading your book.
o: The focus is on the activity — I may not have finished it
I have finished the whole book
I'm going to read it later
items.why: Continuous = the activity; simple (I've read) = the finished result.

items.q: We ___ to Turkistan last summer.
items.why: last summer = finished time → Past Simple. go → went.

items.q: When I was a child, I ___ in a small village.
items.why: A past state (when I was a child) → Past Simple.

items.q: I met Daniyar ___.
items.why: ago marks a finished point in the past → Past Simple.

items.q: Abai Kunanbayev ___ in 1845.
items.why: A definite past date → was/were.

items.q: I ___ out last night — I was too tired.
items.why: Negative: didn't + V1 (go, not went).

items.q: Yesterday I ___ up, had a shower and left for work.
items.why: A sequence of finished actions → Past Simple. get → got.

items.q: They watched the match.
a: They did not watch the match.
items.why: didn't + V1: watch, not watched.

items.q: Aliya passed her exam.
items.why: Did + subject + V1?

items.a: Where did you spend your holiday?
items.why: Wh-word + did + subject + V1?

items.q: Did you saw the news?
items.why: After did → V1: Did you see …?

items.q: She were very tired after the trip.
items.why: I/he/she/it → was; you/we/they → were.

items.q: At 8 p.m. yesterday I ___ dinner.
items.why: In progress at a specific past moment → was/were + -ing.

items.q: I ___ a shower when the phone rang.
items.why: A longer action interrupted by a short one (rang) → was + -ing.

items.q: While I ___ home, it started to rain.
items.why: while + the longer background action → was + -ing.

items.q: The sun ___ and the birds were singing.
items.why: Background description in a story → Past Continuous.

items.q: She was listening to the teacher.
a: She was not listening to the teacher.
items.why: wasn't + -ing.

items.q: They were studying at the library.
a: Were they studying at the library?
items.why: Were + subject + -ing?

items.a: What were you doing at ten o'clock last night?
items.why: A question about a past moment: What + were + you + doing?

items.q: They was playing football in the yard.
items.why: They → were.

items.q: I was walking home when I saw an accident.
o: A longer action interrupted by a short one
Two actions one after the other
items.why: was walking = the background; saw = the short event.

items.q: This time yesterday, I was flying to Astana.
items.why: In progress around a past moment.

items.q: When we got to the cinema, the film ___.
items.why: The film started BEFORE we got there → had + V3.

items.q: She was nervous because she ___ on a plane before.
items.why: never … before up to a past moment → had never + V3.

items.q: By the time the police arrived, the thief ___.
items.why: by the time + past → the earlier action is had + V3.

items.q: I didn't recognise him because he ___ a beard.
items.why: The earlier action explains the past situation → had + V3. grow → grown.

items.q: If we ___ earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train.
items.why: Third conditional: If + had + V3, would have + V3.

items.q: I had seen the film before.
a: I had not seen the film before.
items.why: hadn't + V3.

items.q: They had finished the project by Friday.
a: Had they finished the project by Friday?
items.why: Had + subject + V3?

items.a: I had never eaten sushi before that day.
items.why: had never + V3 … before.

items.q: I was hungry because I didn't eat since breakfast.
items.why: Up to a past moment (since breakfast) → had + V3.

items.q: When I arrived, Dana had left.
o: Dana left before I arrived — I didn't see her
Dana left just after I arrived
Dana was leaving as I arrived
items.why: had left = earlier than my arrival.

items.q: We ___ for two hours when the bus finally came.
items.why: Duration up to a past moment → had been + -ing.

items.q: Her hands were dirty because she ___ in the garden.
items.why: Evidence in the past (dirty hands) of an earlier activity → had been + -ing.

items.q: He was out of breath because he ___.
items.why: An earlier activity explains a past state → had been + -ing.

items.q: The roads were wet. It ___ all night.
items.why: A visible trace of an earlier process → had been + -ing.

items.q: She ___ in Paris for ten years when she decided to move.
items.why: Both are correct with live: the continuous stresses the duration.

items.q: I had been sleeping well before the exams.
a: I had not been sleeping well before the exams.
items.why: hadn't + been + -ing.

items.q: They had been talking for an hour.
a: How long had they been talking?
items.why: How long + had + subject + been + -ing?

items.a: I had been working there for six months when I got a promotion.
items.why: Duration up to a past event → had been + -ing.

items.q: She was tired because she had been work all day.
items.why: had been + -ING: had been working.

items.q: When I arrived, Dana had been crying.
o: Her face showed she had cried before I came
She started crying when I arrived
She cried once in her life
items.why: had been + -ing = an earlier process with visible traces.

items.q: I think Kazakhstan ___ the match tomorrow.
items.why: An opinion about the future (I think) → will + V1.

items.q: The phone's ringing! — Don't get up, I ___ it.
items.why: A decision made at the moment of speaking → will.

items.q: ___ I open the window? It's hot in here.
items.why: Offer with I/we → Shall I …?

items.q: Don't worry, I ___ anyone your secret.
items.why: A promise → won't + V1.

items.q: That bag looks heavy. I ___ you.
items.why: An offer of help → will + V1.

items.q: She will be at home tonight.
a: Will she be at home tonight?
items.why: Will + subject + V1?

items.q: They will finish on time.
a: They will not finish on time.
items.why: won't + V1.

items.a: I'm sure you will pass the exam.
items.why: Prediction with I'm sure → will + V1.

items.q: I will call you when I will get home.
items.why: After when / if / as soon as (future meaning) → Present Simple, not will.

items.q: A: We've run out of milk. B: Oh, I'll buy some on my way home.
o: A decision made at the moment of speaking
items.why: B decides while speaking → will.

items.q: Don't call me at nine — I ___ my driving test then.
items.why: In progress at a future moment (at nine) → will be + -ing.

items.q: This time next week, we ___ on the beach.
items.why: This time next week → will be + -ing. lie → lying.

items.q: At 10 a.m. tomorrow I ___ in a meeting.
items.why: In progress at a future time → will be + -ing.

items.q: When you arrive, the children ___, so please be quiet.
items.why: Background to another future event → will be + -ing.

items.q: I will be working tomorrow evening.
a: I will not be working tomorrow evening.
items.why: won't be + -ing.

items.q: They will be travelling all day.
a: Will they be travelling all day?
Will they be traveling all day?
items.why: Will + subject + be + -ing?

items.a: What will you be doing at this time tomorrow?
items.why: Wh-word + will + subject + be + -ing?

items.q: This time tomorrow I will be fly to Tokyo.
items.why: will be + -ING: will be flying.

items.q: Will you be using the car tonight? I'd like to borrow it.
o: A polite question about someone's plans
A question about a finished action
items.why: Future Continuous makes questions about plans sound polite.

items.q: Don't phone Aliya at 7 — she'll be having dinner.
o: Dinner will be in progress at 7
She has dinner at 7 every day
items.why: will be + -ing = in progress at that moment.

items.q: By Friday, I ___ the report.
items.why: by + a future time → completed before it: will have + V3.

items.q: By the time you get here, we ___ dinner.
items.why: By the time + Present Simple → will have + V3.

items.q: By 2030, they ___ the new bridge.
items.why: Completed before 2030 → will have + V3.

items.q: In June, my parents ___ married for 30 years.
items.why: A total up to a future point → will have been.

items.q: By the end of this course, you ___ all twelve tenses.
items.why: Completed by a deadline → will have + V3.

items.q: She will have arrived by noon.
a: She will not have arrived by noon.
items.why: won't have + V3.

items.q: You will have read the book by Monday.
a: Will you have read the book by Monday?
items.why: Will + subject + have + V3?

items.a: I will have saved enough money by next summer.
items.why: will have + V3 + by …

items.q: By the time he will arrive, we'll have left.
items.why: After by the time (future) → Present Simple: arrives.

items.q: Don't call at 6 — I'll have left the office by then.
o: I will be leaving at exactly 6
items.why: will have + V3 = finished before that moment.

items.q: By next June, I ___ here for ten years.
items.why: Duration up to a future point → will have been + -ing.

items.q: By the time you arrive, I ___ for three hours.
items.why: By the time + Present Simple; duration → will have been + -ing.

items.q: In ten minutes we ___ for an hour!
items.why: How long, up to a future point → will have been + -ing.

items.q: She'll be exhausted when she arrives because she ___ all day.
items.why: The reason for a future state → will have been + -ing.

items.q: By 2030, I ___ three books.
items.why: How MANY (a total) → Future Perfect Simple, not continuous.

items.q: They will have been living here for a year by May.
a: How long will they have been living here by May?
items.why: How long + will + subject + have been + -ing?

items.a: By December, she will have been teaching for twenty years.
items.why: will have been + -ing + for …

items.q: By 5 p.m. I will have been wait for six hours.
items.why: will have been + -ING.

items.q: By June, I'll have been working here for a year.
o: In June, it'll be a year since I started working here
I worked here for a year until June
I start working here in June
items.why: This rare tense is often replaced by a simpler phrase with since.

items.q: By midnight, they'll have been dancing for five hours.
items.why: A process lasting up to a future moment.

items.q: Aliya usually ___ to work, but this week she ___ the bus.
items.why: usually = habit (simple); this week = temporary (continuous).

items.q: Listen! Someone ___ at the door.
items.why: Listen! → happening now.

items.q: I ___ what you mean.
items.why: understand is a state verb → simple.

items.q: Turn off the cooker — the water ___!
items.why: Happening now (not a general fact) → is boiling.

items.q: My dad ___ on Sundays.
items.why: A regular habit → cooks.

items.q: Don't take my umbrella — I ___ it.
items.why: need is a state verb → simple, even about now.

items.q: Why do you laugh? What's so funny?
items.why: About this moment → are you laughing.

items.q: Dana lives with her parents, but this month she's staying with her aunt.
items.why: Simple for permanent, continuous for temporary.

items.q: I ___ Dana yesterday.
items.why: yesterday = finished time → Past Simple.

items.q: We ___ three tests so far this term.
items.why: so far / this term (not finished) → Present Perfect.

items.q: Shakespeare ___ about 39 plays.
items.why: His life is finished → Past Simple.

items.q: I ___ my phone last night, and I still can't find it.
items.why: last night = a definite time → Past Simple, even though the result continues.

items.q: She ___ in Astana since 2020.
items.why: since + a starting point up to now → Present Perfect.

items.q: We ___ to Astana in 2020.
items.why: in 2020 = a finished time → Past Simple.

items.q: I have finished school in 2019.
items.why: in 2019 = definite past time → Past Simple.

items.q: Arman has broken his leg.
o: It's recent news — the leg is still broken
It happened at a time the speaker mentions
items.why: Present Perfect = past action, present result.

items.q: I ___ three cups of coffee today.
items.why: How MANY → Present Perfect Simple.

items.q: How many pages ___ so far?
items.why: How many = a result → simple.

items.q: She ___ him for years.
items.why: know is a state verb → simple.

items.q: Someone ___ my sandwich — the plate is empty!
items.why: Finished result (it's all gone) → has eaten.

items.q: Someone ___ my sandwich — there's only half left!
items.why: Unfinished activity with evidence → has been eating.

items.q: How long ___ English?
items.why: How long + an activity → have you been + -ing.

items.q: We have been owning this car since 2015.
items.why: own is a state verb → have owned.

items.q: Why are your hands so dirty? — I've been fixing the bike.
o: The activity explains the dirty hands; the bike may not be ready
The bike is definitely fixed now
I'm going to fix it later
items.why: Continuous = the activity and its traces, not the result.

items.q: While I ___ dinner, the lights went out.
items.why: while + the longer action in progress → was + -ing.

items.q: I ___ my bag on the bus yesterday.
items.why: A single complete event → Past Simple.

items.q: When the teacher ___, we ___ quietly.
items.why: Short event (came in) + action already in progress (were working).

items.q: It ___ when we left the house, so we took an umbrella.
items.why: The situation in progress at that moment → was raining.

items.q: She ___ and broke her arm while she was skiing.
items.why: The short event that interrupts → Past Simple. fall → fell.

items.q: What ___ when I called you?
items.why: In progress at the moment of the call → were you doing.

items.q: I was meeting an old friend at the market by chance yesterday.
items.why: A short, complete event → met.

items.q: When she arrived, we were having lunch.
o: Lunch had already started when she arrived
We started lunch after she arrived
We finished lunch before she arrived
items.why: were having = already in progress.

items.q: When I got home, my family ___, so I ate alone.
items.why: They ate BEFORE I got home → had eaten.

items.q: First I made a cup of tea, then I ___ the newspaper.
items.why: A sequence in order → Past Simple for each step.

items.q: Everything was white. It ___ during the night.
items.why: Earlier action explains the past situation → had + V3.

items.q: Abai ___ in 1904.
items.why: A single past event, even long ago → Past Simple.

items.q: I couldn't get in because I ___ my key.
items.why: The earlier cause → had + V3.

items.q: I had gone to the cinema yesterday.
items.why: One past event with no earlier-past link → Past Simple.

items.q: The house was quiet when I got back. Everyone has gone to bed.
items.why: Before a past moment (when I got back) → had gone.

items.q: When we arrived at the station, the train had left.
o: The train left the moment we arrived
items.why: had left = before we arrived.

items.q: By noon, she ___ five letters.
items.why: How MANY (result) → Past Perfect Simple.

items.q: They ___ each other for years before they got married.
items.why: know is a state verb → simple.

items.q: I ___ for an hour when the lights went out.
items.why: An activity in progress for a time, interrupted → had been + -ing.

items.q: The ground was wet because it ___.
items.why: Evidence of an earlier process → had been + -ing.

items.q: By the time I got to the station, the train ___.
items.why: A completed action before a past moment → had + V3.

items.q: How long ___ there before he moved?
items.why: had been + -ING.

items.q: She had been finishing the report by 5 p.m., so she went home.
items.why: It was complete → had finished.

items.q: When I came in, Sam had been painting the room.
o: There were signs of painting; it may not be finished
He started painting when I came in
items.why: Continuous = activity and its traces.

title.en: Future forms: will · going to · Present Continuous
title.ru: Будущее: will · going to · Present Continuous
title.kz: Келер шақ: will · going to · Present Continuous

items.q: I'm cold. — Wait, I ___ the window.
items.why: Decision at the moment of speaking → will.

items.q: I ___ my grandmother on Saturday — I've already bought the ticket.
items.why: A fixed arrangement → Present Continuous.

items.q: Look at those black clouds! It ___ rain.
items.why: A prediction from present evidence → be going to.

items.q: I promise I ___ late again.
items.why: Promise → won't.

items.q: Call me when you ___.
items.why: After when (future) → Present Simple.

items.q: If it will rain tomorrow, we'll stay at home.
items.why: After if (future) → Present Simple: rains.

items.q: We're having a party on Saturday.
o: We are at the party now
items.why: Present Continuous for arranged plans.

items.q: The train leaves at 6:15 tomorrow.
items.why: Timetables → Present Simple.

items.q: At 9 p.m. I ___ dinner, so call me later.
items.why: In progress at 9 → will be + -ing.

items.q: Call me at 10 — I ___ dinner by then.
items.why: Finished before 10 (by then) → will have + V3.

intro.en: Present Simple is the ‘calmest’ tense in English. It describes things that happen regularly, things that are always or generally true, and things that follow a timetable. It doesn't mean ‘right now’ — it means ‘in general, usually, as a rule’.
intro.ru: Present Simple — самое «спокойное» время английского. Оно описывает то, что происходит регулярно, что верно всегда или долго, и то, что работает по расписанию. Это не «прямо сейчас», а «вообще, обычно, как правило».
intro.kz: Present Simple — ағылшын тіліндегі ең «сабырлы» шақ. Ол үнемі қайталанып тұратын іс-әрекетті, әрқашан немесе ұзақ уақыт бойы шын болатын нәрсені және кесте бойынша өтетін оқиғаларды білдіреді. Бұл «дәл қазір» емес, «жалпы, әдетте, көбінесе» деген мағына.

keyIdea.en: Present Simple talks about things that happen regularly or are always true: habits, facts and permanent states.
keyIdea.ru: Present Simple говорит о том, что бывает регулярно или верно всегда: привычки, факты, постоянные состояния.
keyIdea.kz: Present Simple үнемі болып тұратын немесе әрқашан шын нәрселер туралы айтады: әдеттер, фактілер, тұрақты күйлер.

text.en: Things we do regularly, out of habit or with a certain frequency. You often see words like *always, usually, every day, twice a week*.
text.ru: То, что мы делаем постоянно, по привычке или с определённой частотой. Часто рядом стоят слова *always, usually, every day, twice a week*.
text.kz: Үнемі, әдет бойынша немесе белгілі бір жиілікпен жасайтын іс-әрекеттеріміз. Жанында көбіне *always, usually, every day, twice a week* сияқты сөздер тұрады.

ex.en: Aruzhan drinks tea with milk every morning.
ex.ru: Аружан каждое утро пьёт чай с молоком.
ex.kz: Аружан күнде таңертең сүт қосылған шай ішеді.

ex.en: We go to the gym three times a week.
ex.ru: Мы ходим в спортзал три раза в неделю.
ex.kz: Біз аптасына үш рет спортзалға барамыз.

text.en: Things that are always true: laws of nature, scientific facts, things everyone knows.
text.ru: То, что верно всегда: законы природы, научные факты, общеизвестные вещи.
text.kz: Әрқашан шын болатын нәрселер: табиғат заңдары, ғылыми фактілер, баршаға белгілі жайттар.

ex.en: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.
ex.ru: Вода замерзает при нуле градусов по Цельсию.
ex.kz: Су нөл градус Цельсийде қатады.

ex.en: The sun rises in the east.
ex.ru: Солнце встаёт на востоке.
ex.kz: Күн шығыстан шығады.

text.en: Things that last a long time and don't feel temporary: where someone lives, what job they do, what they like.
text.ru: То, что длится долго и не воспринимается как временное: где человек живёт, кем работает, что любит.
text.kz: Ұзақ уақытқа созылатын, уақытша деп қабылданбайтын нәрселер: адамның қайда тұратыны, кім болып жұмыс істейтіні, нені ұнататыны.

ex.en: My parents live in Astana.
ex.ru: Мои родители живут в Астане.
ex.kz: Ата-анам Астанада тұрады.

ex.en: He works as an engineer at a big company.
ex.ru: Он работает инженером в большой компании.
ex.kz: Ол үлкен компанияда инженер болып жұмыс істейді.

text.en: Verbs of thinking, feeling and owning (*know, like, want, believe, belong, need*) are usually in the Present Simple, even when we mean ‘now’.
text.ru: Глаголы мыслей, чувств и обладания (*know, like, want, believe, belong, need*) обычно стоят в Present Simple, даже если речь идёт о «сейчас».
text.kz: Ой, сезім және иелік білдіретін етістіктер (*know, like, want, believe, belong, need*) «қазір» туралы айтсақ та, әдетте Present Simple-де тұрады.

ex.en: I know the answer.
ex.ru: Я знаю ответ.
ex.kz: Мен жауапты білемін.

ex.en: This backpack belongs to Dana.
ex.ru: Этот рюкзак принадлежит Дане.
ex.kz: Бұл рюкзак Данаға тиесілі.

text.en: For future events that follow an official timetable: trains, planes, lessons, films, the start of a course.
text.ru: Для будущих событий по официальному расписанию: поезда, самолёты, уроки, фильмы, начало курса.
text.kz: Ресми кесте бойынша болатын келешектегі оқиғалар үшін: пойыздар, ұшақтар, сабақтар, фильмдер, курстың басталуы.

ex.en: The train to Almaty leaves at 8:15 tomorrow.
ex.ru: Поезд в Алматы отправляется завтра в 8:15.
ex.kz: Алматыға баратын пойыз ертең 8:15-те жүреді.

ex.en: Our new course starts on Monday.
ex.ru: Наш новый курс начинается в понедельник.
ex.kz: Біздің жаңа курсымыз дүйсенбіде басталады.

text.en: We use it to give directions or instructions, to tell the story of a film or book, and in live sports commentary.
text.ru: Когда объясняем дорогу или порядок действий, пересказываем сюжет фильма или книги, ведём спортивный комментарий.
text.kz: Жол сілтегенде немесе іс-әрекеттің ретін түсіндіргенде, фильмнің не кітаптың мазмұнын айтып бергенде, спорттық репортаж жүргізгенде.

ex.en: You turn left at the bank and then go straight.
ex.ru: Поворачиваешь налево у банка и потом идёшь прямо.
ex.kz: Банктің тұсынан солға бұрыласың да, тура жүре бересің.

ex.en: In the film, a young girl finds a magic door.
ex.ru: В фильме юная девушка находит волшебную дверь.
ex.kz: Фильмде жас қыз сиқырлы есік тауып алады.

formula.t: V1 (+ s/es with he, she, it)

note.en: With *I, you, we, they* — just V1. With *he, she, it* (and any singular noun) add **-s / -es**: *she works, he watches*. The verb *be* is special: *I am, he is, they are* — no do.
note.ru: С *I, you, we, they* — просто V1. С *he, she, it* (и любым существительным в единственном числе) добавляем **-s / -es**: *she works, he watches*. Глагол *be* особый: *I am, he is, they are* — без do.
note.kz: *I, you, we, they* бастауыштарымен — жай ғана V1. *he, she, it* (және жекеше түрдегі кез келген зат есім) болса, етістікке **-s / -es** жалғанады: *she works, he watches*. *be* етістігі ерекше: *I am, he is, they are* — do керек емес.

ex.en: I play volleyball on Fridays.
ex.ru: Я играю в волейбол по пятницам.
ex.kz: Мен жұма күндері волейбол ойнаймын.

ex.en: She teaches maths at a school in Almaty.
ex.ru: Она преподаёт математику в школе в Алматы.
ex.kz: Ол Алматыдағы бір мектепте математикадан сабақ береді.

ex.en: They live near the park.
ex.ru: Они живут рядом с парком.
ex.kz: Олар саябақтың жанында тұрады.

note.en: *do not = don't*, *does not = doesn't*. After *doesn't* the verb has **no -s**: *he doesn't play* (not *doesn't plays*). The -s ‘moves’ to does. With be, make the negative without do: *She isn't at home.*
note.ru: *do not = don't*, *does not = doesn't*. После *doesn't* глагол **без -s**: *he doesn't play* (не *doesn't plays*). Окончание -s «переходит» в does. Отрицание с be — без do: *She isn't at home.*
note.kz: *do not = don't*, *does not = doesn't*. *doesn't* тұрса, етістік **-s жалғауынсыз** келеді: *he doesn't play* (*doesn't plays* емес). -s жалғауы does сөзіне «көшіп кетеді». be етістігінің болымсыз түрі do-сыз жасалады: *She isn't at home.*

ex.en: I don't eat meat.
ex.ru: Я не ем мясо.
ex.kz: Мен ет жемеймін.

ex.en: My brother doesn't speak Chinese.
ex.ru: Мой брат не говорит по-китайски.
ex.kz: Ағам қытайша сөйлемейді.

ex.en: We don't have lessons on Sundays.
ex.ru: У нас нет уроков по воскресеньям.
ex.kz: Жексенбі күндері бізде сабақ болмайды.

note.en: *Does* is for he/she/it, and then the verb has no -s. In a Wh-question: question word + do/does + subject + V1: *Where do you live?* When the question word is the subject (*Who? What?*), you don't need do: *Who lives here?*
note.ru: *Does* — для he/she/it, и тогда глагол без -s. В Wh-вопросе: вопросительное слово + do/does + subject + V1: *Where do you live?* Если спрашиваем о подлежащем (*Who? What?*), do не нужен: *Who lives here?*
note.kz: *Does* he/she/it үшін қолданылады, сонда етістік -s жалғауынсыз тұрады. Wh-сұрағында: сұрау сөз + do/does + бастауыш + V1: *Where do you live?* Егер бастауыштың өзін сұрасақ (*Who? What?*), do керек емес: *Who lives here?*

ex.en: Do you like horror films?
ex.ru: Тебе нравятся фильмы ужасов?
ex.kz: Саған қорқынышты фильмдер ұнай ма?

ex.en: Does Aliya work on Saturdays?
ex.ru: Алия работает по субботам?
ex.kz: Әлия сенбі күндері жұмыс істей ме?

ex.en: Where do your grandparents live?
ex.ru: Где живут твои бабушка и дедушка?
ex.kz: Атаң мен әжең қайда тұрады?

short: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.
Yes, they do. / No, they don't.

items.en: Usually add **-s**: *work → works*, *play → plays*, *read → reads*
items.ru: Обычно + **-s**: *work → works*, *play → plays*, *read → reads*
items.kz: Әдетте **-s** жалғанады: *work → works*, *play → plays*, *read → reads*

items.en: After -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -z, -o add **-es**: *watch → watches*, *fix → fixes*, *go → goes*, *do → does*
items.ru: После -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -z, -o + **-es**: *watch → watches*, *fix → fixes*, *go → goes*, *do → does*
items.kz: -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -z, -o әріптерінен кейін **-es** жалғанады: *watch → watches*, *fix → fixes*, *go → goes*, *do → does*

items.en: Consonant + y → **-ies**: *study → studies*, *fly → flies*; but vowel + y: *play → plays*, *buy → buys*
items.ru: Согласная + y → **-ies**: *study → studies*, *fly → flies*; но гласная + y: *play → plays*, *buy → buys*
items.kz: Дауыссыз + y → **-ies**: *study → studies*, *fly → flies*; ал дауысты + y болса: *play → plays*, *buy → buys*

items.en: Exception: *have → has*
items.ru: Исключение: *have → has*
items.kz: Ерекше жағдай: *have → has*

items.en: Pronunciation: /s/ *works*, /z/ *plays*, /ɪz/ *watches, uses*
items.ru: Произношение: /s/ *works*, /z/ *plays*, /ɪz/ *watches, uses*
items.kz: Айтылуы: /s/ *works*, /z/ *plays*, /ɪz/ *watches, uses*

items.en: Before the main verb: *She often walks to school.*
items.ru: Перед смысловым глаголом: *She often walks to school.*
items.kz: Негізгі етістіктің алдында: *She often walks to school.*

items.en: After *am / is / are*: *He is always late.*
items.ru: После *am / is / are*: *He is always late.*
items.kz: *am / is / are* етістіктерінен кейін: *He is always late.*

items.en: *Usually, sometimes* can also go at the start of the sentence: *Sometimes we eat out.*
items.ru: *Usually, sometimes* можно поставить в начало: *Sometimes we eat out.*
items.kz: *Usually, sometimes* сөйлемнің басында да тұра алады: *Sometimes we eat out.*

items.en: *every day, once a week, on Mondays* usually go at the end: *I call my mum every day.*
items.ru: *every day, once a week, on Mondays* — обычно в конце: *I call my mum every day.*
items.kz: *every day, once a week, on Mondays* әдетте сөйлемнің соңында тұрады: *I call my mum every day.*

title.en: Present Simple for the future after when / if
title.ru: Present Simple о будущем после when / if
title.kz: when / if сөздерінен кейінгі Present Simple (келешек туралы)

items.en: After *when, if, as soon as, before, after, until* we use the Present Simple for the future, not will
items.ru: После *when, if, as soon as, before, after, until* о будущем ставим Present Simple, а не will
items.kz: *when, if, as soon as, before, after, until* сөздерінен кейін келешек туралы will емес, Present Simple қолданылады

items.en: *Call me when you get home.* (not *when you will get*)
items.ru: *Call me when you get home.* (не *when you will get*)
items.kz: *Call me when you get home.* (*when you will get* емес)

items.en: *If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay at home.*
items.ru: *If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay at home.*
items.kz: *If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay at home.*

note.en: Signal words help, but the meaning decides: *I usually walk to school* (a habit), but *I'm walking to school today because the bus isn't running* (temporary, just today).
note.ru: Слова-сигналы помогают, но решает смысл: *I usually walk to school* (привычка), но *I'm walking to school today because the bus isn't running* (временно, сегодня).
note.kz: Белгі сөздер көмектеседі, бірақ шешуші — мағына: *I usually walk to school* (әдет), ал *I'm walking to school today because the bus isn't running* (уақытша, тек бүгін).

mistakes.wrong: She work in a bank.
mistakes.right: She works in a bank.

why.en: With he/she/it the verb takes **-s**. It's a tiny ending, so it's very easy to forget.
why.ru: С he/she/it глагол получает **-s**. В русском окончание меняется само собой, а в английском его легко забыть.
why.kz: he/she/it бастауышымен етістікке **-s** жалғанады. Бұл кішкентай ғана жалғау, сондықтан оны ұмытып кету оңай.

mistakes.wrong: He doesn't plays tennis.
mistakes.right: He doesn't play tennis.

why.en: The -s is already ‘inside’ *does*. After *doesn't / does*, use the bare V1.
why.ru: Окончание -s уже «сидит» в *does*. После *doesn't / does* — чистый V1.
why.kz: -s жалғауы *does* сөзінің ішінде «отыр». *doesn't / does* тұрса, етістік таза V1 түрінде қолданылады.

mistakes.wrong: Does she likes coffee?
mistakes.right: Does she like coffee?

why.en: In a question with *Does*, the verb has no -s: *Does she like…?*
why.ru: В вопросе с *Does* глагол без -s: *Does she like…?*
why.kz: *Does* арқылы жасалған сұраулы сөйлемде етістік -s жалғауынсыз тұрады: *Does she like…?*

mistakes.wrong: I am agree with you.
mistakes.right: I agree with you.

why.en: In some languages ‘I agree’ sounds like an adjective, but in English *agree* is a verb. *Am* isn't needed.
why.ru: По-русски «я согласен» звучит как прилагательное, но *agree* — это глагол. *Am* не нужен.
why.kz: Қазақшадағы «келісемін» сияқты, *agree* да — етістік. Сондықтан *Am* қажет емес.

mistakes.wrong: Where you live?
mistakes.right: Where do you live?

why.en: An English question needs the auxiliary *do/does*. You can't just add a question word or change your intonation.
why.ru: В английском вопросе нужен вспомогательный глагол *do/does*. Нельзя просто поменять интонацию, как в русском.
why.kz: Ағылшын тіліндегі сұраулы сөйлемге *do/does* көмекші етістігі керек. Қазақшадағыдай сұрау сөзді қоя салу жеткіліксіз.

mistakes.wrong: My friend don't like rap.
mistakes.right: My friend doesn't like rap.

why.en: *My friend* = he/she, so it's *doesn't*.
why.ru: *My friend* = he/she, значит *doesn't*.
why.kz: *My friend* = he/she, сондықтан *doesn't* қолданылады.

mistakes.wrong: I am work at a café.
mistakes.right: I work at a café.

why.en: Don't mix *am* with V1. Say either *I work* (Present Simple) or *I am working* (Present Continuous).
why.ru: Нельзя смешивать *am* и V1. Либо *I work* (Present Simple), либо *I am working* (Present Continuous).
why.kz: *am* мен V1-ді араластыруға болмайды. Не *I work* (Present Simple), не *I am working* (Present Continuous).

text.en: Present Simple is for permanent, regular, ‘in general’ things. Present Continuous is for what's happening now or for a limited time.
text.ru: Present Simple — постоянное, регулярное, «вообще». Present Continuous — то, что происходит сейчас или временно.
text.kz: Present Simple — тұрақты, үнемі болатын, «жалпы» нәрселер. Present Continuous — қазір болып жатқан немесе уақытша нәрселер.

a.en: Dana lives with her parents.

b.en: Dana is staying with her aunt this month.

text.en: When we say **how long** something has lasted up to now (*for / since*), we need the Present Perfect, not the Present Simple — even if your language uses the present tense here.
text.ru: Когда говорим, **как долго** что-то длится до сейчас (*for / since*), нужен Present Perfect, а не Present Simple, хотя по-русски мы говорим в настоящем времени.
text.kz: Бір нәрсенің қазірге дейін **қанша уақытқа** созылғанын айтқанда (*for / since*), қазақшада осы шақ қолданылса да, ағылшын тілінде Present Simple емес, Present Perfect керек.

a.en: I live in Astana.

b.en: I've lived in Astana for five years.

review.en: Present Simple is for habits, facts, permanent states and timetables.
review.ru: Present Simple — для привычек, фактов, постоянных состояний и расписаний.
review.kz: Present Simple — әдеттер, фактілер, тұрақты күйлер мен кестелер үшін.

review.en: With *he / she / it* add **-s / -es** to the verb: *she works, he watches, it goes*.
review.ru: С *he / she / it* к глаголу добавляем **-s / -es**: *she works, he watches, it goes*.
review.kz: *he / she / it* бастауыштарымен етістікке **-s / -es** жалғанады: *she works, he watches, it goes*.

review.en: Negative: *don't / doesn't + V1*; after *doesn't* there's no -s.
review.ru: Отрицание: *don't / doesn't + V1*; после *doesn't* окончание -s не нужно.
review.kz: Болымсыз түр: *don't / doesn't + V1*; *doesn't* тұрса, -s жалғауы керек емес.

review.en: Question: *Do / Does + subject + V1?* Wh-question: *Where do you live?*
review.ru: Вопрос: *Do / Does + subject + V1?* В Wh-вопросе: *Where do you live?*
review.kz: Сұраулы түр: *Do / Does + subject + V1?* Wh-сұрағында: *Where do you live?*

review.en: State verbs (*know, like, want, believe*) are usually in the Present Simple.
review.ru: Глаголы состояния (*know, like, want, believe*) обычно стоят в Present Simple.
review.kz: Күй етістіктері (*know, like, want, believe*) әдетте Present Simple-де тұрады.

review.en: After *when, if, as soon as*, use the Present Simple for the future: *when he arrives*.
review.ru: После *when, if, as soon as* о будущем — Present Simple: *when he arrives*.
review.kz: *when, if, as soon as* сөздерінен кейін келешек туралы Present Simple қолданылады: *when he arrives*.

review.en: *Agree* is a verb: *I agree*, not *I am agree*.
review.ru: *Agree* — глагол: *I agree*, а не *I am agree*.
review.kz: *Agree* — етістік: *I am agree* емес, *I agree*.

timeline.en: People in Kazakhstan celebrate Nauryz in March.
timeline.ru: В Казахстане празднуют Наурыз в марте.
timeline.kz: Қазақстанда Наурызды наурыз айында тойлайды.

timeline.en: My grandma bakes baursaks every Saturday.
timeline.ru: Моя бабушка каждую субботу печёт баурсаки.
timeline.kz: Әжем сенбі сайын бауырсақ пісіреді.

timeline.en: The library closes at eight.
timeline.ru: Библиотека закрывается в восемь.
timeline.kz: Кітапхана сағат сегізде жабылады.

timeline.en: Marat runs five kilometres every morning.
timeline.ru: Марат каждое утро пробегает пять километров.
timeline.kz: Марат күнде таңертең бес шақырым жүгіреді.

timeline.en: Dana paints in the park at weekends.
timeline.ru: Дана по выходным рисует в парке.
timeline.kz: Дана демалыс күндері саябақта сурет салады.

timeline.en: Cats sleep for most of the day.
timeline.ru: Кошки спят большую часть дня.
timeline.kz: Мысықтар күннің көп бөлігін ұйқымен өткізеді.

tagline.en: Right now and for a while

intro.en: Present Continuous shows an action in progress: it's happening now, at the moment of speaking, or during this period of life. We also use it for things that are changing and for plans we have already arranged.
intro.ru: Present Continuous показывает действие в процессе: оно идёт сейчас, в момент речи, или в этот период жизни. Ещё им говорят о том, что меняется, и о планах, о которых уже договорились.
intro.kz: Present Continuous үдерістегі іс-әрекетті көрсетеді: ол қазір, сөйлеп тұрған сәтте немесе өмірдің осы кезеңінде болып жатыр. Сондай-ақ ол өзгеріп жатқан нәрселер мен алдын ала келісіп қойған жоспарлар туралы айтқанда қолданылады.

keyIdea.en: Present Continuous is an action in progress: now, during a temporary period, or as an arrangement for the near future.
keyIdea.ru: Present Continuous — действие в процессе: сейчас, в этот временный период или по договорённости в ближайшем будущем.
keyIdea.kz: Present Continuous — үдерістегі іс-әрекет: қазір, уақытша кезеңде немесе жақын болашаққа келісілген жоспар бойынша.

text.en: The action is happening at the moment of speaking and hasn't finished yet. Common signals: *now, right now, at the moment, Look!, Listen!*
text.ru: Действие происходит в момент речи и ещё не закончилось. Часто рядом: *now, right now, at the moment, Look!, Listen!*
text.kz: Іс-әрекет сөйлеп тұрған сәтте болып жатыр және әлі аяқталған жоқ. Жиі қатар келетін сөздер: *now, right now, at the moment, Look!, Listen!*

ex.en: Look! It's snowing.
ex.ru: Смотри! Идёт снег.
ex.kz: Қара! Қар жауып тұр.

ex.en: Daniyar is talking on the phone at the moment.
ex.ru: Данияр сейчас разговаривает по телефону.
ex.kz: Данияр қазір телефонмен сөйлесіп тұр.

text.en: Things happening around this time (not necessarily this second) that will end soon: *this week, this month, these days*.
text.ru: То, что происходит в этот период (не обязательно в эту секунду) и скоро закончится: *this week, this month, these days*.
text.kz: Осы кезеңде болып жатқан (міндетті түрде дәл осы секундта емес) және жақында аяқталатын нәрселер: *this week, this month, these days*.

ex.en: I'm staying with my aunt in Astana this month.
ex.ru: В этом месяце я живу у тёти в Астане.
ex.kz: Осы айда мен Астанада тәтемнің үйінде тұрып жатырмын.

ex.en: Aliya is learning to drive these days.
ex.ru: Алия сейчас учится водить машину.
ex.kz: Әлия қазір көлік жүргізуді үйреніп жүр.

text.en: A situation is gradually changing: something is growing, getting better or becoming different. Typical verbs: *get, become, change, grow, improve, rise*.
text.ru: Ситуация постепенно меняется: что-то растёт, улучшается, становится другим. Типичные глаголы: *get, become, change, grow, improve, rise*.
text.kz: Жағдай біртіндеп өзгеріп келеді: бірдеңе өсіп, жақсарып немесе басқаша бола бастайды. Жиі қолданылатын етістіктер: *get, become, change, grow, improve, rise*.

ex.en: Almaty is getting bigger every year.
ex.ru: Алматы с каждым годом становится больше.
ex.kz: Алматы жыл сайын үлкейіп келеді.

ex.en: Your English is improving!
ex.ru: Твой английский становится лучше!
ex.kz: Ағылшын тілің жақсарып келеді!

text.en: Personal plans that are already arranged (you've bought tickets or agreed on a time). Usually there's a time expression: *tomorrow, on Friday, at six*.
text.ru: Личные планы, о которых уже договорились (купили билеты, назначили встречу). Обычно указано время: *tomorrow, on Friday, at six*.
text.kz: Алдын ала келісіп қойған жеке жоспарлар (билет алынған, кездесу уақыты белгіленген). Әдетте уақыты көрсетіледі: *tomorrow, on Friday, at six*.

ex.en: We're meeting Marat at the cinema at six.
ex.ru: Мы встречаемся с Маратом в кинотеатре в шесть.
ex.kz: Біз Маратпен сағат алтыда кинотеатрда кездесеміз.

ex.en: I'm flying to Shymkent on Friday.
ex.ru: В пятницу я лечу в Шымкент.
ex.kz: Жұма күні мен Шымкентке ұшамын.

text.en: With *always, constantly, forever*, it shows a repeated action that annoys or surprises the speaker.
text.ru: С *always, constantly, forever* показывает повторяющееся действие, которое раздражает или удивляет говорящего.
text.kz: *always, constantly, forever* сөздерімен бірге келіп, сөйлеушінің ашуын келтіретін немесе таңғалдыратын қайталанатын әрекетті білдіреді.

ex.en: He's always losing his keys!
ex.ru: Он вечно теряет ключи!
ex.kz: Ол кілттерін үнемі жоғалтып ала береді!

ex.en: You're constantly interrupting me.
ex.ru: Ты постоянно меня перебиваешь.
ex.kz: Сен менің сөзімді үнемі бөле бересің.

note.en: *I am*, *he / she / it is*, *you / we / they are* + V-ing. In speech we use short forms: *I'm, she's, they're*. You need both parts: *be* and *-ing*.
note.ru: *I am*, *he / she / it is*, *you / we / they are* + V-ing. В разговоре сокращаем: *I'm, she's, they're*. Оба элемента обязательны: и *be*, и *-ing*.
note.kz: *I am*, *he / she / it is*, *you / we / they are* + V-ing. Ауызекі сөйлеуде қысқартамыз: *I'm, she's, they're*. Екі бөлік те міндетті: *be* және *-ing*.

ex.en: I'm reading a great book.
ex.ru: Я читаю отличную книгу.
ex.kz: Мен керемет кітап оқып жатырмын.

ex.en: She is cooking plov for the whole family.
ex.ru: Она готовит плов для всей семьи.
ex.kz: Ол бүкіл отбасына палау пісіріп жатыр.

ex.en: They're playing football in the yard.
ex.ru: Они играют в футбол во дворе.
ex.kz: Олар аулада футбол ойнап жатыр.

note.en: Short forms: *I'm not*, *isn't*, *aren't* (or *he's not, they're not*). There is no form *amn't*.
note.ru: Сокращения: *I'm not*, *isn't*, *aren't* (или *he's not, they're not*). Формы *amn't* нет.
note.kz: Қысқартылған түрлері: *I'm not*, *isn't*, *aren't* (немесе *he's not, they're not*). *amn't* деген түр жоқ.

ex.en: I'm not sleeping, I'm just resting.
ex.ru: Я не сплю, я просто отдыхаю.
ex.kz: Мен ұйықтап жатқан жоқпын, жай демалып жатырмын.

ex.en: He isn't working today.
ex.ru: Он сегодня не работает.
ex.kz: Ол бүгін жұмыс істеп жатқан жоқ.

ex.en: We aren't watching TV.
ex.ru: Мы не смотрим телевизор.
ex.kz: Біз теледидар көріп отырған жоқпыз.

note.en: Put *am / is / are* before the subject. In a Wh-question: question word + am/is/are + subject + V-ing: *What are you doing?*
note.ru: Ставим *am / is / are* перед подлежащим. В Wh-вопросе: вопросительное слово + am/is/are + subject + V-ing: *What are you doing?*
note.kz: *am / is / are* бастауыштың алдына қойылады. Wh-сұрағында: сұрау сөз + am/is/are + бастауыш + V-ing: *What are you doing?*

ex.en: Are you listening to me?
ex.ru: Ты меня слушаешь?
ex.kz: Сен мені тыңдап отырсың ба?

ex.en: Is Dana painting in the park?
ex.ru: Дана рисует в парке?
ex.kz: Дана саябақта сурет салып жүр ме?

ex.en: What are you doing right now?
ex.ru: Что ты делаешь прямо сейчас?
ex.kz: Дәл қазір не істеп жатырсың?

short: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
Yes, he is. / No, he isn't.
Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.

items.en: Usually add **-ing**: *read → reading*, *play → playing*
items.ru: Обычно + **-ing**: *read → reading*, *play → playing*
items.kz: Әдетте **-ing** жалғанады: *read → reading*, *play → playing*

items.en: A silent -e is dropped: *make → making*, *write → writing* (but *be → being*, *see → seeing*)
items.ru: Немая -e исчезает: *make → making*, *write → writing* (но *be → being*, *see → seeing*)
items.kz: Соңындағы оқылмайтын -e түсіп қалады: *make → making*, *write → writing* (бірақ *be → being*, *see → seeing*)

items.en: -ie → **-ying**: *lie → lying*, *die → dying*
items.ru: -ie → **-ying**: *lie → lying*, *die → dying*
items.kz: -ie → **-ying**: *lie → lying*, *die → dying*

items.en: Double the final consonant when the last syllable is stressed and ends in one vowel + one consonant: *run → running*, *swim → swimming*, *begin → beginning*
items.ru: Удваиваем конечную согласную, если последний слог ударный и кончается на одну гласную + одну согласную: *run → running*, *swim → swimming*, *begin → beginning*
items.kz: Соңғы буын екпінді болып, бір дауысты + бір дауыссызбен аяқталса, соңғы дауыссыз екі еселенеді: *run → running*, *swim → swimming*, *begin → beginning*

items.en: Don't double it if the last syllable isn't stressed: *visit → visiting*, *open → opening*; but British English has *travel → travelling* (American *traveling*)
items.ru: Не удваиваем без ударения: *visit → visiting*, *open → opening*; но в британском *travel → travelling* (амер. *traveling*)
items.kz: Соңғы буын екпінсіз болса, еселенбейді: *visit → visiting*, *open → opening*; бірақ британ ағылшынында *travel → travelling* (америкалық нұсқада *traveling*)

items.en: Usually **not** used in the Continuous: *know, understand, believe, like, love, hate, want, need, prefer, belong, own, seem, mean, remember*
items.ru: Обычно **не** в Continuous: *know, understand, believe, like, love, hate, want, need, prefer, belong, own, seem, mean, remember*
items.kz: Әдетте Continuous түрінде **қолданылмайды**: *know, understand, believe, like, love, hate, want, need, prefer, belong, own, seem, mean, remember*

items.en: *I know him.* (not *I'm knowing him*), *I need help now.* (not *I'm needing*)
items.ru: *I know him.* (не *I'm knowing him*), *I need help now.* (не *I'm needing*)
items.kz: *I know him.* (*I'm knowing him* емес), *I need help now.* (*I'm needing* емес)

items.en: *think*: *I think it's a good idea* (opinion) — *I'm thinking about the test* (considering it)
items.ru: *think*: *I think it's a good idea* (мнение) — *I'm thinking about the test* (обдумываю)
items.kz: *think*: *I think it's a good idea* (пікір) — *I'm thinking about the test* (ойланып жүрмін)

items.en: *have*: *She has a car* (possession) — *She's having lunch* (an action: eating lunch)
items.ru: *have*: *She has a car* (владеет) — *She's having lunch* (действие: обедает)
items.kz: *have*: *She has a car* (иелік) — *She's having lunch* (әрекет: түскі ас ішіп отыр)

items.en: *see*: *I see what you mean* (understand) — *I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow* (have an appointment)
items.ru: *see*: *I see what you mean* (понимаю) — *I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow* (встречаюсь)
items.kz: *see*: *I see what you mean* (түсінемін) — *I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow* (кездесемін, қабылдауына барамын)

items.en: *taste*: *This soup tastes great* (state) — *He's tasting the soup* (trying it)
items.ru: *taste*: *This soup tastes great* (состояние) — *He's tasting the soup* (пробует)
items.kz: *taste*: *This soup tastes great* (күй) — *He's tasting the soup* (дәмін татып көріп жатыр)

note.en: Signal words help, but meaning comes first: state verbs stay in the Present Simple even with *now*: *I understand it now* (not *I'm understanding*).
note.ru: Сигналы помогают, но смысл важнее: глаголы состояния остаются в Present Simple даже с *now*: *I understand it now* (не *I'm understanding*).
note.kz: Белгі сөздер көмектеседі, бірақ мағына маңыздырақ: күй етістіктері *now* сөзімен келсе де Present Simple-де қалады: *I understand it now* (*I'm understanding* емес).

mistakes.wrong: She cooking dinner now.
mistakes.right: She is cooking dinner now.

why.en: Learners often drop *is*, because many languages don't need a word like it here. Present Continuous needs **both** parts: *am/is/are* + V-ing.
why.ru: В русском нет связки «есть», поэтому *is* часто теряется. В Present Continuous нужны **оба** элемента: *am/is/are* + V-ing.
why.kz: Қазақ тілінде *is* сияқты жеке байламдық сөз жоқ, сондықтан ол жиі түсіп қалады. Present Continuous-қа **екі** бөлік те керек: *am/is/are* + V-ing.

mistakes.wrong: I'm knowing the answer.
mistakes.right: I know the answer.

why.en: *Know* is a state verb, so it isn't usually used in the Continuous.
why.ru: *Know* — глагол состояния, в Continuous обычно не используется.
why.kz: *Know* — күй етістігі, ол әдетте Continuous түрінде қолданылмайды.

mistakes.wrong: Are you understand me?
mistakes.right: Do you understand me?

why.en: *Understand* is a state verb, so use the Present Simple and a question with *Do*. Never mix *are* with V1.
why.ru: *Understand* — глагол состояния, поэтому Present Simple и вопрос с *Do*. Смешивать *are* и V1 нельзя.
why.kz: *Understand* — күй етістігі, сондықтан Present Simple және *Do* арқылы жасалған сұрақ керек. *are* мен V1-ді араластыруға болмайды.

mistakes.wrong: Look! The bus come.
mistakes.right: Look! The bus is coming.

why.en: *Look!* tells us the action is happening right now, so we need the Present Continuous.
why.ru: *Look!* показывает, что действие происходит прямо сейчас — нужен Present Continuous.
why.kz: *Look!* әрекеттің дәл қазір болып жатқанын көрсетеді — Present Continuous керек.

mistakes.wrong: I am wanting a new phone.
mistakes.right: I want a new phone.

why.en: *Want* is a state verb (it describes a wish, not an action), so use the Present Simple.
why.ru: *Want* — глагол желания (состояния), поэтому Present Simple.
why.kz: *Want* — қалау білдіретін күй етістігі, сондықтан Present Simple қолданылады.

mistakes.wrong: He is swiming in the pool.
mistakes.right: He is swimming in the pool.

why.en: One stressed vowel + one consonant → double the consonant: *swim → swimming*.
why.ru: Одна ударная гласная + одна согласная → согласная удваивается: *swim → swimming*.
why.kz: Бір екпінді дауысты + бір дауыссыз → дауыссыз екі еселенеді: *swim → swimming*.

mistakes.wrong: What do you do now?
mistakes.right: What are you doing now?

why.en: *What do you do?* means ‘What's your job?’. To ask about an action at this moment, say *What are you doing?*
why.ru: *What do you do?* значит «Кем ты работаешь?». О действии в эту минуту — *What are you doing?*
why.kz: *What do you do?* «Кім болып жұмыс істейсің?» дегенді білдіреді. Дәл осы сәттегі әрекет туралы — *What are you doing?*

text.en: Present Continuous is for what's happening now or temporarily. Present Simple is for regular, permanent, ‘in general’ things.
text.ru: Present Continuous — то, что идёт сейчас или временно. Present Simple — регулярное, постоянное, «вообще».
text.kz: Present Continuous — қазір немесе уақытша болып жатқан нәрсе. Present Simple — үнемі болатын, тұрақты, «жалпы» нәрсе.

a.en: Dana is painting a sunset right now.

b.en: Dana paints every weekend.

text.en: About the future: Present Continuous is a personal plan that's already arranged. *Will* is a decision made at the moment of speaking, or a guess.
text.ru: О будущем: Present Continuous — личный план, о котором уже договорились. *Will* — решение в момент речи или предположение.
text.kz: Келешек туралы: Present Continuous — алдын ала келісілген жеке жоспар. *Will* — сөйлеп тұрған сәтте қабылданған шешім немесе болжам.

a.en: I'm visiting my grandparents on Saturday.

b.en: Maybe I'll visit my grandparents on Saturday.

review.en: Form: *am / is / are + V-ing*. Don't forget *am / is / are*!
review.ru: Форма: *am / is / are + V-ing*. Не забывай *am / is / are*!
review.kz: Жасалуы: *am / is / are + V-ing*. *am / is / are* дегенді ұмытпа!

review.en: Actions right now: *now, at the moment, Look!*
review.ru: Действие прямо сейчас: *now, at the moment, Look!*
review.kz: Дәл қазіргі әрекет: *now, at the moment, Look!*

review.en: Temporary situations: *this week, these days*.
review.ru: Временная ситуация: *this week, these days*.
review.kz: Уақытша жағдай: *this week, these days*.

review.en: Change: *is getting, are rising, is improving*.
review.ru: Изменения: *is getting, are rising, is improving*.
review.kz: Өзгерістер: *is getting, are rising, is improving*.

review.en: Future arrangements: *I'm meeting Dana tomorrow.*
review.ru: Будущее по договорённости: *I'm meeting Dana tomorrow.*
review.kz: Келісілген болашақ жоспар: *I'm meeting Dana tomorrow.*

review.en: *always* + Continuous = annoyance: *You're always forgetting!*
review.ru: *always* + Continuous = раздражение: *You're always forgetting!*
review.kz: *always* + Continuous = наразылық: *You're always forgetting!*

review.en: State verbs (*know, like, want, need*) aren't usually used in the Continuous; *think, have, see* have two meanings.
review.ru: Глаголы состояния (*know, like, want, need*) обычно не в Continuous; у *think, have, see* — два значения.
review.kz: Күй етістіктері (*know, like, want, need*) әдетте Continuous түрінде келмейді; *think, have, see* етістіктерінің екі мағынасы бар.

timeline.en: Look, Dana is painting the mountains!
timeline.ru: Смотри, Дана рисует горы!
timeline.kz: Қара, Дана таулардың суретін салып жатыр!

timeline.en: Marat is training for a big race this month.
timeline.ru: В этом месяце Марат готовится к большому забегу.
timeline.kz: Марат осы айда үлкен жарысқа дайындалып жүр.

timeline.en: The city is changing very fast.
timeline.ru: Город меняется очень быстро.
timeline.kz: Қала өте тез өзгеріп жатыр.

timeline.en: Daniyar is having lunch with his friends right now.
timeline.ru: Данияр сейчас обедает с друзьями.
timeline.kz: Данияр қазір достарымен түскі ас ішіп отыр.

timeline.en: We're flying to Astana on Monday.
timeline.ru: В понедельник мы летим в Астану.
timeline.kz: Дүйсенбі күні біз Астанаға ұшамыз.

timeline.en: Aruzhan is reading a book about Abai at the moment.
timeline.ru: Аружан сейчас читает книгу об Абае.
timeline.kz: Аружан қазір Абай туралы кітап оқып отыр.

intro.en: Present Perfect is a bridge between the past and the present. The action has already happened (or has continued since some point), but what matters is its result or its link to ‘now’, not the exact time in the past.
intro.ru: Present Perfect — мост между прошлым и настоящим. Действие уже случилось (или длится с какого-то момента), но нам важен его результат или связь с «сейчас», а не точное время в прошлом.
intro.kz: Present Perfect — өткен шақ пен осы шақтың арасындағы көпір. Іс-әрекет болып қойған (немесе белгілі бір сәттен бері созылып келеді), бірақ бізге оның өткендегі нақты уақыты емес, нәтижесі немесе «қазірмен» байланысы маңызды.

keyIdea.en: Present Perfect connects the past with the present: what matters is the result, the experience or the period ‘up to now’, not exactly when it happened.
keyIdea.ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое с настоящим: важен результат, опыт или период «до сейчас», а не когда именно это было.
keyIdea.kz: Present Perfect өткенді қазірмен байланыстырады: оның дәл қашан болғаны емес, нәтижесі, тәжірибесі немесе «қазірге дейінгі» кезең маңызды.

text.en: Whether something has ever happened in your life (without saying when). Often with *ever, never, before, once, twice*.
text.ru: Было ли это когда-нибудь в жизни (без указания, когда). Часто с *ever, never, before, once, twice*.
text.kz: Өмірде бір нәрсе болған-болмағаны (қашан екені айтылмайды). Көбіне *ever, never, before, once, twice* сөздерімен келеді.

ex.en: Have you ever been to Turkestan?
ex.ru: Ты когда-нибудь был в Туркестане?
ex.kz: Сен бұрын Түркістанда болып көрдің бе?

ex.en: I've never tried horse riding.
ex.ru: Я никогда не пробовал кататься на лошади.
ex.kz: Мен ешқашан ат мініп көрген емеспін.

title.en: A past action with a result now

text.en: The action happened in the past, but its result is visible or important now.
text.ru: Действие в прошлом, но его результат виден или важен сейчас.
text.kz: Іс-әрекет өткенде болған, бірақ оның нәтижесі қазір көрініп тұр немесе қазір маңызды.

ex.en: I've lost my keys, so I can't open the door.
ex.ru: Я потерял ключи, поэтому не могу открыть дверь.
ex.kz: Мен кілттерімді жоғалтып алдым, сондықтан есікті аша алмаймын.

ex.en: Dana has broken her arm.
ex.ru: Дана сломала руку (рука сейчас в гипсе).
ex.kz: Дана қолын сындырып алды (қолы қазір гипсте).

title.en: From the past until now: for / since
title.ru: С прошлого до сейчас: for / since

text.en: A situation started in the past and is still true now. This is especially common with state verbs (*be, know, have, live*). Many languages use the present tense here (‘I know’, ‘I live’), but English uses the Present Perfect.
text.ru: Ситуация началась в прошлом и продолжается сейчас. Особенно с глаголами состояния (*be, know, have, live*). По-русски тут настоящее время — «знаю», «живу».
text.kz: Жағдай өткенде басталып, әлі жалғасып келеді. Әсіресе күй етістіктерімен (*be, know, have, live*) жиі қолданылады. Қазақшада мұнда осы шақ айтылады: «білеміз», «тұрады».

ex.en: We've known each other since school.
ex.ru: Мы знаем друг друга со школы.
ex.kz: Біз бір-бірімізді мектептен бері білеміз.

ex.en: My parents have lived in Astana for ten years.
ex.ru: Мои родители живут в Астане десять лет.
ex.kz: Ата-анам Астанада он жылдан бері тұрады.

title.en: News and recent events: just, already, yet
title.ru: Новости и недавние события: just, already, yet
title.kz: Жаңалықтар мен жақында болған оқиғалар: just, already, yet

text.en: We give fresh news, or say whether something we expected has happened yet.
text.ru: Сообщаем свежую новость или говорим, случилось ли уже ожидаемое.
text.kz: Жаңа ғана болған жаңалықты хабарлаймыз немесе күткен нәрсенің болған-болмағанын айтамыз.

ex.en: I've just finished my homework.
ex.ru: Я только что закончил домашку.
ex.kz: Мен үй тапсырмамды жаңа ғана бітірдім.

ex.en: Has the parcel arrived yet?
ex.ru: Посылка уже пришла?
ex.kz: Сәлемдеме келіп қойды ма?

title.en: Unfinished time: today, this week, this year
title.ru: Незаконченный период: today, this week, this year
title.kz: Аяқталмаған кезең: today, this week, this year

text.en: The time period isn't over yet, and the action may happen again.
text.ru: Период времени ещё не закончился, и действие может повториться.
text.kz: Уақыт кезеңі әлі аяқталған жоқ, сондықтан әрекет тағы қайталануы мүмкін.

ex.en: I've drunk three cups of coffee today.
ex.ru: Сегодня я выпил три чашки кофе.
ex.kz: Бүгін мен үш кесе кофе іштім.

ex.en: Marat has scored five goals this season.
ex.ru: В этом сезоне Марат забил пять голов.
ex.kz: Осы маусымда Марат бес гол соқты.

text.en: After *It's / This is the first (second…) time* we use the Present Perfect, not the Present Simple.
text.ru: После *It's / This is the first (second…) time* используем Present Perfect, а не Present Simple.
text.kz: *It's / This is the first (second…) time* тіркесінен кейін Present Simple емес, Present Perfect қолданылады.

ex.en: It's the first time I've eaten Chinese hotpot.
ex.ru: Я впервые ем китайский хого.
ex.kz: Мен қытайдың хого тағамын алғаш рет жеп отырмын.

note.en: *Has* is for he/she/it, *have* is for everyone else. V3 is the third form of the verb: regular verbs add *-ed* (*worked*); irregular ones you have to learn (*seen, gone, written*). Short forms: *I've, she's, they've*.
note.ru: *Has* — для he/she/it, *have* — для остальных. V3 — третья форма глагола: у правильных *-ed* (*worked*), неправильные учим (*seen, gone, written*). Сокращения: *I've, she's, they've*.
note.kz: *Has* he/she/it үшін, *have* қалғандары үшін қолданылады. V3 — етістіктің үшінші формасы: дұрыс етістіктерде *-ed* (*worked*), ал бұрыс етістіктерді жаттап алу керек (*seen, gone, written*). Қысқартылған түрлері: *I've, she's, they've*.

ex.en: I've been to Kazan twice.
ex.ru: Я был в Казани два раза.
ex.kz: Мен Қазанда екі рет болдым.

ex.en: She has finished her project.
ex.ru: Она закончила свой проект.
ex.kz: Ол өз жобасын аяқтады.

ex.en: We've bought new laptops for the office.
ex.ru: Мы купили новые ноутбуки для офиса.
ex.kz: Біз кеңсеге жаңа ноутбуктер сатып алдық.

note.en: *have not = haven't*, *has not = hasn't*. You can also make a negative with *never*: *I've never seen it*.
note.ru: *have not = haven't*, *has not = hasn't*. Отрицание можно выразить и через *never*: *I've never seen it*.
note.kz: *have not = haven't*, *has not = hasn't*. Болымсыздықты *never* арқылы да білдіруге болады: *I've never seen it*.

ex.en: I haven't seen this film.
ex.ru: Я не смотрел этот фильм.
ex.kz: Мен бұл фильмді көрген жоқпын.

ex.en: Arman hasn't called me yet.
ex.ru: Арман мне ещё не позвонил.
ex.kz: Арман маған әлі хабарласқан жоқ.

ex.en: They haven't decided where to go.
ex.ru: Они ещё не решили, куда поехать.
ex.kz: Олар қайда баратынын әлі шешкен жоқ.

note.en: *Have / Has* moves to the front. Don't use the Present Perfect with *When…?* — ask in the Past Simple: *When did you arrive?*
note.ru: *Have / Has* выходит вперёд. С *When…?* Present Perfect не используем — спрашиваем в Past Simple: *When did you arrive?*
note.kz: *Have / Has* сөйлемнің басына шығады. *When…?* сұрағымен Present Perfect қолданылмайды — Past Simple-мен сұраймыз: *When did you arrive?*

ex.en: Have you done your homework?
ex.ru: Ты сделал домашнее задание?
ex.kz: Үй тапсырмаңды орындадың ба?

ex.en: Has Dana sold any paintings?
ex.ru: Дана продала хоть одну картину?
ex.kz: Дана суреттерінің бірін болса да сатты ма?

ex.en: How long have you known Aruzhan?
ex.ru: Как давно ты знаешь Аружан?
ex.kz: Аружанды қашаннан бері білесің?

short: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
Yes, she has. / No, she hasn't.

items.en: Regular verbs: V2 = V3 = **-ed**: *work → worked → worked*, *study → studied → studied*
items.ru: Правильные глаголы: V2 = V3 = **-ed**: *work → worked → worked*, *study → studied → studied*
items.kz: Дұрыс етістіктер: V2 = V3 = **-ed**: *work → worked → worked*, *study → studied → studied*

items.en: Irregular verbs have to be learnt: *go → went → gone*, *see → saw → seen*, *write → wrote → written*
items.ru: Неправильные нужно учить: *go → went → gone*, *see → saw → seen*, *write → wrote → written*
items.kz: Бұрыс етістіктерді жаттау керек: *go → went → gone*, *see → saw → seen*, *write → wrote → written*

items.en: Sometimes V2 = V3: *buy → bought → bought*, *make → made → made*
items.ru: Иногда V2 = V3: *buy → bought → bought*, *make → made → made*
items.kz: Кейде V2 = V3: *buy → bought → bought*, *make → made → made*

items.en: The Present Perfect always uses V3: *I have seen* (not *I have saw*)
items.ru: В Present Perfect только V3: *I have seen* (не *I have saw*)
items.kz: Present Perfect-те тек V3 қолданылады: *I have seen* (*I have saw* емес)

items.en: *She has gone to Astana.* — she went there and is there now
items.ru: *She has gone to Astana.* — уехала и сейчас там
items.kz: *She has gone to Astana.* — кетті және қазір сонда

items.en: *She has been to Astana.* — she went there (experience) and has come back
items.ru: *She has been to Astana.* — была там (опыт) и уже вернулась
items.kz: *She has been to Astana.* — барып, қайтып оралған (тәжірибе)

items.en: For experience, use *been*: *Have you ever been to China?*
items.ru: Для опыта используем *been*: *Have you ever been to China?*
items.kz: Тәжірибе туралы айтқанда *been* қолданамыз: *Have you ever been to China?*

items.en: *for* + a period: *for two years, for ages, for a long time*
items.ru: *for* + период: *for two years, for ages, for a long time*
items.kz: *for* + кезең: *for two years, for ages, for a long time*

items.en: *since* + a starting point: *since 2020, since Monday, since I was a child*
items.ru: *since* + точка начала: *since 2020, since Monday, since I was a child*
items.kz: *since* + басталу нүктесі: *since 2020, since Monday, since I was a child*

items.en: *just, already* go between have and V3: *I've just eaten*; *yet* goes at the end of a question or negative
items.ru: *just, already* — между have и V3: *I've just eaten*; *yet* — в конце вопроса или отрицания
items.kz: *just, already* have мен V3-тің арасында тұрады: *I've just eaten*; *yet* сұраулы не болымсыз сөйлемнің соңында тұрады

items.en: **Not** with finished time: *yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago* → Past Simple
items.ru: **Не** с законченным временем: *yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago* → Past Simple
items.kz: Аяқталған уақытпен **қолданылмайды**: *yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago* → Past Simple

note.en: The key question is whether the time is finished: *I've seen Dana today* (the day isn't over yet), but *I saw Dana yesterday* (yesterday is over).
note.ru: Главное — закончилось ли время: *I've seen Dana today* (день ещё идёт), но *I saw Dana yesterday* (вчера уже закончилось).
note.kz: Ең бастысы — уақыттың аяқталған-аяқталмағаны: *I've seen Dana today* (күн әлі біткен жоқ), ал *I saw Dana yesterday* (кеше өтіп кетті).

mistakes.wrong: I have seen him yesterday.
mistakes.right: I saw him yesterday.

why.en: *Yesterday* is finished time. Use the Past Simple with it, never the Present Perfect.
why.ru: *Yesterday* — законченное время. С ним только Past Simple, Present Perfect нельзя.
why.kz: *Yesterday* — аяқталған уақыт. Онымен тек Past Simple қолданылады, Present Perfect қолдануға болмайды.

mistakes.wrong: I know him since 2020.
mistakes.right: I've known him since 2020.

why.en: Many languages use the present here, but in English a period ‘from the past until now’ needs the Present Perfect.
why.ru: По-русски «знаю с 2020», но в английском период «с прошлого до сейчас» требует Present Perfect.
why.kz: Қазақшада «2020 жылдан бері білемін» деп осы шақпен айтамыз, бірақ ағылшын тілінде «өткеннен қазірге дейінгі» кезең Present Perfect-ті талап етеді.

mistakes.wrong: We live here since 3 years.
mistakes.right: We've lived here for three years.

why.en: Two mistakes at once: you need the Present Perfect, and with a period you use *for*. *Since* only goes with a starting point (*since 2023*).
why.ru: Две ошибки сразу: нужен Present Perfect, а с периодом — *for*. *Since* ставим только с точкой начала (*since 2023*).
why.kz: Бірден екі қате: Present Perfect керек, ал кезеңмен *for* қолданылады. *Since* тек басталу нүктесімен келеді (*since 2023*).

mistakes.wrong: Did you ever try kazy?
mistakes.right: Have you ever tried kazy?

why.en: A question about life experience uses the Present Perfect. (*Did you ever…?* is heard in American English, but the British standard is *Have you ever…?*)
why.ru: Вопрос об опыте «за всю жизнь» — Present Perfect. (*Did you ever…?* встречается в американском английском, но в британском стандарт — *Have you ever…?*)
why.kz: «Бүкіл өмірдегі» тәжірибе туралы сұрақ — Present Perfect. (*Did you ever…?* америкалық ағылшын тілінде кездеседі, бірақ британ нұсқасында стандарт — *Have you ever…?*)

mistakes.wrong: She has went to Astana.
mistakes.right: She has gone to Astana.

why.en: After *has* you need V3: *go → went → gone*. *Went* is V2.
why.ru: После *has* нужна V3: *go → went → gone*. *Went* — это V2.
why.kz: *has* сөзінен кейін V3 керек: *go → went → gone*. *Went* — бұл V2.

mistakes.wrong: When have you arrived?
mistakes.right: When did you arrive?

why.en: *When* asks about a specific time in the past, so use the Past Simple.
why.ru: *When* спрашивает о конкретном времени в прошлом — это Past Simple.
why.kz: *When* өткендегі нақты уақытты сұрайды — бұл Past Simple.

mistakes.wrong: This is the first time I visit Almaty.
mistakes.right: This is the first time I've visited Almaty.

why.en: After *This is the first time*, use the Present Perfect — even though many languages use the present tense here.
why.ru: После *This is the first time* — Present Perfect, хотя по-русски мы говорим «впервые приезжаю».
why.kz: *This is the first time* тіркесінен кейін Present Perfect қолданылады, қазақшада «Алматыға алғаш рет келіп тұрмын» деп осы шақпен айтсақ та.

text.en: Present Perfect: the result now matters and no time is given. Past Simple: an action in finished past time, often with the time stated.
text.ru: Present Perfect — важен результат сейчас, время не названо. Past Simple — действие в законченном прошлом, часто с указанием времени.
text.kz: Present Perfect — қазіргі нәтиже маңызды, уақыт айтылмайды. Past Simple — аяқталған өткендегі әрекет, көбіне уақыты көрсетіледі.

a.en: I've lost my phone.

b.en: I lost my phone last week.
b.kz: Қашан болғаны маңызды; уақыт өтіп кетті.

text.en: Present Perfect: result and quantity (how much is done). Present Perfect Continuous: process and duration (how long you've been doing it).
text.ru: Present Perfect — результат и количество (сколько сделано). Present Perfect Continuous — процесс и длительность (сколько времени занимался).
text.kz: Present Perfect — нәтиже мен саны (қаншасы істелді). Present Perfect Continuous — үдеріс пен ұзақтығы (қанша уақыт айналысты).

a.en: I've written three emails.

b.en: I've been writing emails all morning.

review.en: Form: *have / has + V3*. Learn the irregular verbs: *gone, seen, done, written*.
review.ru: Форма: *have / has + V3*. Учи неправильные глаголы: *gone, seen, done, written*.
review.kz: Жасалуы: *have / has + V3*. Бұрыс етістіктерді жатта: *gone, seen, done, written*.

review.en: Experience: *Have you ever…? I've never…*
review.ru: Опыт: *Have you ever…? I've never…*
review.kz: Тәжірибе: *Have you ever…? I've never…*

review.en: Result now: *I've lost my keys.*
review.ru: Результат сейчас: *I've lost my keys.*
review.kz: Қазіргі нәтиже: *I've lost my keys.*

review.en: From the past until now: *for* + a period, *since* + a starting point: *I've known her since 2019.*
review.ru: С прошлого до сейчас: *for* + период, *since* + точка начала: *I've known her since 2019.*
review.kz: Өткеннен қазірге дейін: *for* + кезең, *since* + басталу нүктесі: *I've known her since 2019.*

review.en: News: *just, already, yet*.
review.ru: Новости: *just, already, yet*.
review.kz: Жаңалықтар: *just, already, yet*.

review.en: **Never** with *yesterday, ago, last…, in 2019* or in questions with *When…?* — use the Past Simple there.
review.ru: **Никогда** с *yesterday, ago, last…, in 2019* и в вопросах с *When…?* — там Past Simple.
review.kz: *yesterday, ago, last…, in 2019* сөздерімен және *When…?* сұрағында **ешқашан** қолданылмайды — онда Past Simple керек.

review.en: *been* = went and came back, *gone* = went and is still there.
review.ru: *been* = был и вернулся, *gone* = уехал и ещё там.
review.kz: *been* = барып қайтты, *gone* = кетті және әлі сонда.

timeline.en: I've visited Shymkent three times.
timeline.ru: Я был в Шымкенте три раза.
timeline.kz: Мен Шымкентте үш рет болдым.

timeline.en: Dana has just passed her driving test.
timeline.ru: Дана только что сдала экзамен по вождению.
timeline.kz: Дана көлік жүргізу емтиханын жаңа ғана тапсырды.

timeline.en: We've had this cat since 2022.
timeline.ru: У нас эта кошка с 2022 года.
timeline.kz: Бұл мысық бізде 2022 жылдан бері бар.

timeline.en: Marat has never lost a race.
timeline.ru: Марат ни разу не проигрывал забег.
timeline.kz: Марат жарыста бірде-бір рет жеңілген емес.

timeline.en: Dana has painted twenty pictures this year.
timeline.ru: В этом году Дана нарисовала двадцать картин.
timeline.kz: Осы жылы Дана жиырма сурет салды.

timeline.en: Oh no, I've forgotten my student card!
timeline.ru: О нет, я забыл студенческий!
timeline.kz: Ой, студенттік билетімді ұмытып кетіппін!

intro.en: Present Perfect Continuous talks about a process that started in the past and continues up to now (or has only just stopped). It answers the question ‘how long?’ and explains why we can see signs of some activity now.
intro.ru: Present Perfect Continuous рассказывает о процессе, который начался в прошлом и длится до сейчас (или только что закончился). Он отвечает на вопрос «как долго?» и объясняет, почему сейчас видны следы какого-то занятия.
intro.kz: Present Perfect Continuous өткенде басталып, қазірге дейін созылып келе жатқан (немесе жаңа ғана тоқтаған) үдеріс туралы айтады. Ол «қанша уақыттан бері?» деген сұраққа жауап береді және қандай да бір істің ізі қазір неге көрініп тұрғанын түсіндіреді.

keyIdea.en: Present Perfect Continuous is a process from the past up to now: what matters is how long the action has been going on, or what someone has been doing.
keyIdea.ru: Present Perfect Continuous — процесс с прошлого до сейчас: важно, как долго длится действие или чем человек занимался.
keyIdea.kz: Present Perfect Continuous — өткеннен қазірге дейінгі үдеріс: әрекеттің қанша уақыттан бері созылып келе жатқаны немесе адамның немен айналысқаны маңызды.

title.en: How long an action has been going on
title.ru: Как долго длится действие до сейчас
title.kz: Әрекеттің қазірге дейін қанша уақыт созылғаны

text.en: The action started in the past and is still going on. Often with *for, since, How long…?, all day*. Many languages use the present tense here, but English uses the Present Perfect Continuous.
text.ru: Действие началось в прошлом и всё ещё продолжается. Часто с *for, since, How long…?, all day*. По-русски тут настоящее время: «учу уже четыре года».
text.kz: Әрекет өткенде басталған және әлі жалғасып жатыр. Көбіне *for, since, How long…?, all day* сөздерімен келеді. Қазақшада мұнда осы шақ қолданылады: «төрт жылдан бері оқып жүрмін».

ex.en: I've been learning English for four years.
ex.ru: Я учу английский уже четыре года.
ex.kz: Мен ағылшын тілін төрт жылдан бері үйреніп жүрмін.

ex.en: How long have you been waiting?
ex.ru: Сколько ты уже ждёшь?
ex.kz: Қанша уақыттан бері күтіп тұрсың?

title.en: A recent process with visible signs

text.en: The action has recently stopped (or is still going on), and we can see the signs: wet streets, red eyes, tiredness.
text.ru: Действие недавно закончилось (или ещё продолжается), и мы видим его следы: мокрые улицы, красные глаза, усталость.
text.kz: Әрекет жақында ғана аяқталған (немесе әлі жалғасып жатыр), біз оның ізін көреміз: дымқыл көшелер, қызарған көздер, шаршау.

ex.en: The streets are wet. It has been raining.
ex.ru: Улицы мокрые. Шёл дождь.
ex.kz: Көшелер дымқыл. Жаңбыр жауған екен.

ex.en: Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?
ex.ru: У тебя красные глаза. Ты плакал?
ex.kz: Көздерің қызарып кетіпті. Жыладың ба?

text.en: Something has been happening regularly over a recent period. Often with *lately, recently*.
text.ru: Что-то происходит регулярно в последний период. Часто с *lately, recently*.
text.kz: Соңғы кезеңде бір нәрсе үнемі қайталанып жүр. Көбіне *lately, recently* сөздерімен келеді.

ex.en: I've been going to the gym a lot lately.
ex.ru: В последнее время я часто хожу в спортзал.
ex.kz: Соңғы кезде мен спортзалға жиі барып жүрмін.

ex.en: Marat has been training every morning recently.
ex.ru: В последнее время Марат тренируется каждое утро.
ex.kz: Соңғы уақытта Марат күнде таңертең жаттығып жүр.

text.en: What matters is the activity itself, not the result; the action may not be finished yet. If the result or the quantity matters, use the Present Perfect.
text.ru: Нам важна сама деятельность, а не её итог; действие может быть ещё не закончено. Если важен результат или количество — Present Perfect.
text.kz: Бізге іс-әрекеттің нәтижесі емес, өзі маңызды; әрекет әлі аяқталмауы да мүмкін. Нәтиже немесе саны маңызды болса — Present Perfect.
